echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Duplication gate (production JS duplicated lines <= 1%, ratcheted)
        # Ratchet, not an absolute bar: a pinned set of production JS files
        # already exceeds 1% duplicated lines — pre-existing debt owned by the
        # gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets (see duplication-baseline.json for the
        # current pinned set) — so the measurement's exit 2 is expected for
        # now. The baseline pins each over-threshold file with its measured
        # percentage and absolute duplicated-line count; the gate FAILS only
        # on a NEW over-threshold file or a pinned file that gained ABSOLUTE
        # duplicated lines (ci/duplicationRatchet.js) — a percentage shift
        # caused by file shrinkage passes and is logged as informational —
        # keeping the absolute 1% bar as the end state once the debt lands.
        # A crashed measurement (tool exit other than 0/2) never passes.
        # js/unit-tests/** stays excluded; the badge step below reparses the
        # same measurement for the README endpoint.
        run: |
          set +e
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci > "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" 2>&1
          code=$?
          set -e
          node ci/duplicationRatchet.js "$RUNNER_TEMP/dup-gate.txt" duplication-baseline.json "$code"

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Duplication gate (gh-1251): a second, independent gate fails PRs and main on
# NEW or GROWING JS duplication. The measurement is
# `crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci`; a
# pinned set of production files already exceeds 1% today (pre-existing debt
# owned by the gh-1244…gh-1250 dedup tickets — see duplication-baseline.json
# for the current pinned set), so the gate is a RATCHET against that
# baseline, not an absolute bar — it fails only when a file over threshold is
# not pinned or a pinned file gained ABSOLUTE duplicated lines
# (ci/duplicationRatchet.js; percentage shifts from file shrinkage are
# informational, not failures). Its clones-mode report also feeds the README
# `duplication` endpoint badge published from the same run.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.

content.text:
[epic] Review-thread dispositions: every review thread reaches a terminal state (policy config + 4-tier severity + dispositions + debt ledger)
## Incident (why now)

[PR #1319](https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1319) (merged 2026-11-02T16:14:39Z): the machine review posted **3 unresolved threads** — 1 arguable 🚨-grade correctness finding filed as ⚠️ IMPORTANT ("`buildLabelRuleMap` first-wins drops a lane needle; the shipped `sm.json` hits this today"), 2 💡 — then labeled `pr_approved` + `ai_pr_reviewed`, removed `agent:review`, and merged 2 minutes later. The threads remain unresolved permanently.

Root causes, all verified in code:

1. `allowApproveWithSuggestions: true` + `review_verdict_rules.md` treat ⚠️/💡 as merge-neutral by design (`decideApproval`, `postPRReviewComments.js:1194`).
2. The merge path has **no unresolved-thread gate** — `mergeTrigger.js` and machine SM `decideApprovedGreenActions()` merge `pr_approved` + green + `CLEAN` without checking threads; the gh-828 resolution leg fires only on `mergeState=BLOCKED`, which requires the "require conversation resolution" branch protection this repo lacks (no protection on `main`).
3. **Marker corruption:** thread 1 was posted as `🚨 severity: none — ⚠️ **IMPORTANT…**` — `threadSeverity()` tests 🚨 first → misclassifies as *blocking*; on a conversation-gate repo that thread would be permanently stuck (resolution skips it, rework arm withheld on APPROVE+census 0).
4. The census cross-check promised in `review_verdict_rules.md` ("machine cross-checks the counter against your inline comments before honoring a blocking-0 approval") **is not implemented**.
5. Schema/code mismatch: output schema `suggestion` (singular) vs `hasAnyOpenIssue()`/`normalizeIssueCounts()` reading `suggestions` (plural).

## Agreed policy (owner directive, 2026-11-02)

**Every review thread must reach a terminal resolved state — invariant, not configurable.** Resolution ≠ fixed: small things may be resolved without a fix; everything above nit/small must be fixed. Everything else is per-repo configurable (§1). Default preset:

| Severity | Triggers a lap? | Fixed? | If no lap runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🚨 BLOCKING | Yes — REQUEST_CHANGES | Mandatory | — |
| ⚠️ IMPORTANT | Yes — REQUEST_CHANGES | Mandatory (or justified downgrade) | — |
| 💡 SUGESTION | Only as a bounded polish lap | Yes | polish lap or defer-to-ledger |
| 🪶 NIT | **Never** | Opportunistic (rides any running lap) | triage-resolve with ack |

## 1. Repo policy config — `reviewPolicy` in `.dmtools/config.js`

```javascript
reviewPolicy: {
  preset: 'default',   // 'default' | 'fix-everything' | 'relaxed' | 'investigation'
  severities: {
    BLOCKING:  { round: 'rework', fix: 'mandatory' },
    IMPORTANT: { round: 'rework', fix: 'mandatory' },
    SUGESTION: { round: 'polish', fix: 'mandatory' },
    NIT:       { round: 'none',   fix: 'oportunistic' }
  },
  bounds: { polishMaxThreads: 6, polishMaxChangedLines: 80,
            opportunisticMaxThreads: 8, opportunisticSameFilesOnly: true,
            densityBase: 2, densityK: 3, densityUnit: 200, densityMin: 2, densityMax: 8,
            sweepBatch: 10, sweepMaxAgeDays: 30 }
}
```

- **Presets:** `default` (above) · `fix-everything` (nits always fixed — `round:'polish', fix:'mandatory'`) · `relaxed` (suggestions optional) · `investigation` (all tiers `round:'none', fix:'never'` — reviews are pure signal, triage closes everything incl. 🚨).
- **Resolution chain:** `projectConfig.reviewPolicy` → workflow jobParams → built-in `default`. Missing → default, silent. Malformed (unknown tier, bad enum) → hard validation error at leg start — looseness must be explicit, never a parse accident.
- **Non-configurable invariants:** (a) every thread reaches terminal disposition — no knob; (b) deferred requires its ledger item (receipt rule, §4); (c) human-authored threads are never machine-resolved (gh-744).
- **Owner responsibility:** every tier incl. BLOCKING may be weakened by explicit config — the config IS the owner's standing approval (agent-only repos: "it compiles and runs" is the bar).
- **Legacy knobs reconcile:** `allowApproveWithSuggestions`, `importantBlocksApproval`, `maxReviewThreadsBeforeForceApprove` become derived from (or rejected alongside) the policy.
- **Plumbing:** the effective policy is stamped into review/rework/triage run contexts; `postPRReviewComments` **recomputes the approval mechanically from census + policy** — the model is advisory, the machine is the enforcer.

## 2. Integrity prerequisites (must land first — everything reads markers)

- Machine-stamp each thread's severity line from the structured JSON `severity` field — never trust comment-file prose (kills the `🚨 severity: none` class).
- `threadSeverity()` ordering: explicit `severity: X` word beats emoji; blocking requires 🚨 **and** the word BLOCKING.
- Census cross-check: any posted BLOCKING severity with `issueCounts.blocking == 0` → override verdict to REQUEST_CHANGES + loud log.
- Normalize `suggestion`/`suggestions`; census gains `nits` and `digest` counts.

## 3. Verdict layer

- 4-tier severity enum in **all four review legs at once** (owner decision — no staging): `pr_review.json`, `pr_test_automation_review.json`, `pr_story_test_automation_review.json`, `pr_bug_test_automation_review.json` + `few_shots.md` boundary: *a nit changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented; a suggestion changes clarity of documented/behavioral surface*.
- IMPORTANT gates approval (REQUEST_CHANGES by default); `armReworkDecision()` arms on `important > 0`.

- Escape hatch: rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️→💡 **only with written justification in the census**; `maxReworkRounds` + one owner escalation bounds the loop.

## 4. Disposition protocol

- **Opportunistic pickup:** a lap that runs for 🚨/⚠️ picks up cheap 💡/🪶 in the same files (bounded ≤8 threads). One lap, one commit, all tiers.
- **Triage path** (generalize gh-828 beyond mergeState=BLOCKED): after APPROVE with census clean in lap-gated tiers, resolve machine-owned threads with ack replies carrying machine-parsed tags: `fixed` / `wontfix: <reason>` / `duplicate: #n` / `deferred: #ledger` / `fixed: <ref>`. Closability is policy-driven.
- **Bounded polish lap** for suggestion-only rounds: single commit, ≤6 threads, ≤80 lines, doc/test-trivial fixes; overflow → triage.
- **Density control** (calibrated 2026-11-02):
  `allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3 * sqrt(additions / 200)), 2, 8)` → 20→3 · 50→4 · 200→5 · 800→8.
  Overflow: reviewer posts top-K threads, remainder becomes a ranked digest list in the review comment. 🚨/⚠️ never capped. Anchors: own corpus 19 machine PRs (advisory median 2 / p90 4 / max 8; formula caps 0/19), SmartBear/Cisco 200-line cliff, gh-828 fleet pathology (4–13 threads/PR) bounded at 8. Machine side audits (warn), never fails the leg. Quarterly re-fit.
- **Debt ledger + sweep (the ONLY deferred path — per-finding deferral is banned):** deferring a finding to its own issue triggers the full analyze→fix→PR→review flow per finding — more expensive than fixing in-PR. Instead: ONE rolling `[debt-ledger] <repo>` issue, machine-parsed sections `{fid, severity, originPr, threadUrl, date, text}`, deduped via the finding-identity registry. Sweep trigger: ≥10 items OR oldest ≥30 days → ONE bounded sweep leg → one PR fixing the batch; stale items re-validated against current code and dropped with a note; items failing twice → split out as a real issue (expensive path, now justified). Fail-closed: ledger append failure → thread stays open, retry next tick.
- **Merge backstop:** threads still open ≥⚠️ at merge time → ONE digest issue (severity, path:line, thread links), threads resolved `deferred`, then merge. Nothing unresolved, nothing forgotten.
- **Infra (last):** enable "require conversation resolution" branch protection on `main` — activates the designed BLOCKED path (gh-828 + gh-807). Only after §2 lands, else a corrupt marker permanently BLOCKs approved heads.

## Implementation order (updated 2026-11-04)

**Shipped via child issues (merged):** #1330 (R5 honest reporting) -> #1332 (R10 registry) ->
#1329 (R1 attribution core) -> #1345 (R1 completion: differential dispatcher, role stamping,
machineAuthor guard) -> #1331 (R6 re-check + alternation detector/suppression — residues
confirmed and implemented, lap-by-lap evidence in PR #1348) -> #1334 (R8 demotion provenance).

**Remaining implementation — 4 sequential parts, tracked as sub-issues below:**

1. **#1350** — review-marker integrity (mechanical, merge-safe; no dry-run needed).
2. **#1351** — `reviewPolicy` config + verdict layer (4-tier severity, IMPORTANT gates approval,
   density control). **Dry-run required before live.**
3. **#1352** — disposition loop (opportunistic pickup, triage beyond BLOCKED, bounded polish lap +
   instability budget, review-side ledger generalization). **Dry-run required.**
4. **#1353** — merge backstop (digest issue on unresolved >=IMPORTANT machine threads).

**#1333** (R9 convergence instrumentation) unblocks after #1351 + the polish-lap piece of #1352
land (registry #1332 already shipped); it may run parallel to #1353.

**Owner checklist (not agent work):** branch protection "require conversation resolution" on
`main` — enable ONLY after parts 1-4 are live (permanent-BLOCKED trap otherwise). Per phase-2
agreement: dry-run every behavior-changing part in the test repo before live.

## Rollout## Rollout

1. §2 integrity → 2. §1 config + §3 verdict layer → 3. opportunistic pickup → 4. triage path → 5. polish lap → 6. debt ledger + sweep → 7. merge backstop → 8. branch protection (owner action).

## Acceptance replays

- **#1319 replay:** ⚠️ → REQUEST_CHANGES → lap fixes → 0 open threads → APPROVE → merge. No unresolved thread ever.
- Nit-only: APPROVE, zero legs, both threads ack-resolved. · `fix-everything`: nit-only runs polish lap, nits `fixed`. · `relaxed`: suggestion-only APPROVEs, triage closes. · `investigation`: 🚨 auto-closed by triage via config, no legs.
- Corruption replay: `🚨 severity: none` marker + blocking=0 → cross-check overrides; thread not triage-closable.
- Config validation: unknown tier → leg fails loudly; missing config → default silent.
- Density: 10 💡 on 50-line diff → 2 threads + 8 digest; 1 💡 on 1000 lines → untouched.
- Ledger/sweep: 12 deferred across 9 PRs → sweep at 10-item trigger → ONE PR fixes 8, drops 2 stale; zero per-finding issues.
- Defer fail-closed: ledger append 403 → thread stays open, retries.
- Human thread: never machine-resolved; owner notified. · Cap: unfixable ⚠️ → exactly one escalation after maxReworkRounds.

## Decisions log (owner, 2026-11-02)

1. BLOCKING opt-out per repo config; machine auto-closes; config = owner's standing approval.
2. Density overflow → cap + digest list.
3. Density formula → investigated sub-linear (above), replacing provisional head numbers.
4. Deferred = batched ledger only (addendum: per-finding deferral banned on cost).
5. Rollout: all four review legs at once.
Minor defaults (configurable): opportunistic pickup same-files-only; one digest issue per PR.

## Review notes

This epic consolidates the full fix plan for owner review. Please add requirements/updates as comments. After approval this splits into implementation issues: (1) integrity, (2) config + verdict layer, (3) dispositions + ledger/sweep, (4) backstop + infra.

        # Wave 2 (owner 2026-10-01): teammate packs are self-sufficient —

58:`github.workflow_ref` (runners/scripts always match the invoked ref). The

## 6. The legs (runners)

| Runner | Model | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `fa-bug-dev.json` / `fa-story-dev.json` | z.ai glm | reads the issue body as spec, TDD, PR + summary |
| `fa-review-kimi.json` | kimi (queue head) | reviews the linked PR; posts verdict comment + labels; formal `APPROVE` when tokens allow (own-PR → falls back to labels) |
| `fa-rework-zai.json` | z.ai glm | reads review threads + CI logs, fixes, re-pushes |
| `retry_merge_github.json` | — (deterministic) | squash-merge + issue close + comment |

Review queue (provider failover) is configured in the runner's
`envVariables`: `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE="$ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE"` (where `ENV_VAR_REVIEW_QUEUE='[{"provider_type":"openai-completions","provider_config":{"baseUrl":"https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1","model":"k2p5","apiKeyEnv":"KIMI_CODE_KEY"}},{"provider_type":"zai","provider_config":{"model":"glm-5.3","apiKeyEnv":"ZAI_CODE_KEY"}}]'`)
— first healthy provider wins.

All runners share the `timerAutoCommitAndSave` WIP timer (5 min commits,
`[skip ci]`-able — see §9) and tracker-aware comment formatting
(`commentMarkup.js`: jira wiki vs markdown by ticket-key shape).

---

## 7. What each tick does (deterministic SM)

1. Load rules (pack → `.dmtools/config.js` deep-merge).
2. For each rule: query the carrier (issues / PRs), filter by guards,
   sort FIFO, apply `limit`.
3. For each item: skip if a leg is already in flight for it; dispatch the
   leg (workflow_dispatch with the ticket key + leg) or execute locally
   (merge/labels).
4. Emit `{"success":true,"processed":N,...}` and exit. Ticks are cheap
   (seconds, no LLM).

---

## 8. Troubleshooting (field-tested)

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Legs never fire from labels | labels added with `GITHUB_TOKEN` don't emit events | use `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` PAT in legs; SM re-fires dead letters anyway |
| SM tick dies instantly, `Bad substitution` | script run via `sh` (dash) | call installers with `bash` |
| `github_*` tools "not found" in tick | `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` not in the job env → tools not exposed | add env to the reconcile job |

      review) runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review" ;;
      dev)

        if echo "$title" | grep -qiE '^\[?bug\]' \
          || echo "$LABELS" | grep -qwi "bug"; then
          runner="$RUNNER_BUG"; slot="bug"

          runner="$RUNNER_STORY"; slot="story"
        fi
        ;;
    esac
  elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:rework" \
    && ! echo "$LABELS" | grep -q 'status:In Rework'; then
    # status:In Rework = a rework leg already runs/ran — its own
    # status transition echoes back as a `labeled` event and would
    # re-derive the same leg on top of itself.
    # #544: manual agent:rework is the owner override — it fires
    # rework even from a `labeled` event, but only when the labeler
    # has write/admin (see rework_override_ok). Without permission
    # the override is ignored (runner stays empty → clean skip).
    if rework_override_ok; then
      runner="$RUNNER_REWORK"
    fi
  elif echo "$LABELS" | grep -qw "agent:review"; then
    # status:In Review is NOT an in-flight marker here — the DEV leg
    # sets it as the "ready for review" invitation, so blocking on it
    # kills the label-echo review trigger (live: dmtools-dart gh-182).
    # Real duplicate protection is the per-issue concurrency group.
    runner="$RUNNER_REVIEW"; slot="review"

So in the dry-run I must replicate that: my scripted provider's pr needs `headSha: HEAD`, and the scenario must call `planActionFields`... it's not exported. Instead the scenario can stamp the fields itself: `actions.forEach(a => { a.prNumber = 99; a.headSha = HEAD; })` — miroring planActionFields. Let me patch the script accordingly.

arguments.content:
# gh-1352 — integration readiness concerns

## 1. The `polish` leg has no executor yet (dispatch path only)

- **What the PR does:** the machine SM disposition loop (`js/machineSmAgent.js`)
  dispatches `leg: 'polish'` via `github_trigger_workflow` on `ai-teammate.yml` and stamps
  the per-head `dmtools:polish-lap` marker (once-per-head + instability-budget memory).
  `polish` was added to the workflow's `leg` choice options in this PR — without it GitHub
  rejects the `workflow_dispatch` as an invalid choice.
- **What is missing:** the leg itself. The factory dispatch gate
  (`scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh`, repo **IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows**) resolves
  `INPUT_LEG` with a hardcoded `rework|review|dev` case — an unknown leg leaves the runner
  empty and the run skips as a clean no-op. This repo also has no polish runner: `.dmtools/config.js`
  `sm.runners` carries only bug/story/review/rework, and there is no executor job that reads
  the lap plan (the marker's `resolvedThreadIds`) and applies the ≤6-thread, ≤80-line,
  doc/test-trivial single commit.
- **What is needed to make it work:**
  1. a `polish)` case in the agentic-workflows gate script mapping to a `polish` runner slot;
  2. a `sm.runners.polish` entry in `.dmtools/config.js` pointing at a new
     `.dmtools/runers/fa-polish.json` whose parent job applies the bounded plan
     (the dispatch marker already carries head + top-K thread ids + overflow count).
  Until then every polish dispatch is a logged no-op run — triage still resolves the threads
  (fail-safe: the loop never wedges), so no deadlock is possible.

## 2. The live test-deployment dry-run is an owner-side rollout step

- **What the PR does:** attaches code-level dry-run evidence
  (`outputs/dry-run-gh-1352.md`, re-runnable via `node scripts/dry-run-disposition-loop.js`)
  covering triage, polish, and the full approve-with-suggestions cycle through the real
  `machineSmAgent` decision + execution paths against an in-memory provider.
- **What is missing:** the ticket's behavior-change gate says "dry-run in a non-production
  test deployment required before live". No non-production deployment (test repo + machine_sm
  credentials) is provisioned in this environment — the machine_sm `dryRun: true` knob exists
  (`machine_sm.json` jobParams), but pointing it at a test repo is an owner/config action.
- **What is needed:** run `machine_sm.json` with `jobParams.dryRun: true` against a test
  deployment (a scratch repo with machine-authored review threads) and attach the tick log;
  then flip to live.

Unblocked the stalled gh-1352 disposition-loop leg (suite was red — ~75 failed dev legs): repaired the scope-4a `ledgerCore` extraction fallout (`LEDGERCORE` references left dangling by a WIP auto-save in `test_smAgent.js`/`test_developBugAndCreatePR.js`, plus the missing `ledgerCore` block in `runLocalAction`'s sandbox), closed two live gaps in the polish-lap dispatch (the per-head `dmtools:polish-lap` marker is now stamped **before** the leg dispatch — without it once-per-head and the 2-lap instability budget never tripped — and `dispatchLeg` now carries the issue number, not the issue object), added `polish` to the `ai-teammate.yml` leg choice (GitHub rejects unlisted dispatch choices), deduped the ledger family below the duplication gate (canonical `ledgerFromPayload`/`ledgerRecordOf`/resolve pipeline in `ledgerCore.js`), and added `scripts/dry-run-disposition-loop.js` producing the ticket's acceptance dry-run evidence (triage / polish / full approve-with-suggestions cycle through the real decision+execution paths).

### Key decisions
- Marker-first dispatch: a lap whose marker post fails stays home and falls open to triage — an unstamped lap cannot honour once-per-head, so the loop can never double-lap.
- `postPrComment` joins the polish-gate primitive checks; missing primitives degrade to triage (fail-safe, never wedged).
- Ledger dedup keeps one canonical payload/record/resolve core in `ledgerCore.js`; TC and review-debt faces delegate.

### How to verify
```bash
FILES=$(node -e 'console.log(require("./js/unit-tests/run_all.json").params.jobParams.testFiles.join(" "))')
node js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js $FILES          # 8546 passed, 0 failed
node scripts/dry-run-disposition-loop.js              # acceptance replays, exit 0
node ci/duplicationRatchet.js <(crap4js duplicates --threshold 1 --exclude "js/unit-tests/**" js ci) duplication-baseline.json 2   # OK
```

Dry-run evidence: `outputs/dry-run-gh-1352.md` (leg artifact). Integration concerns (external factory gate case + polish runner/executor, live test-deployment dry-run): `outputs/concerns.md`.

```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| OWNED{"Violations you must fix (N owned) table at the top?"} OWNED -->|Yes| FIX_OWNED["Fix EVERY owned violation (path:line, rule, measured vs limit)
— an owned violation may NOT be dismissed as unrelated/
not caused by this PR/infra; dispute per item with disputed: <reason> only
when the gate itself is wrong"] OWNED -->|No| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] FIX_OWNED --> THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see the TDD approach section included later in this prompt — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P8["8️⃣ input/TICKET/review_policy.md — the resolved reviewPolicy: which severities trigger this lap, density cap, downgrade protocol (gh-1351)"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 --> P8 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify the rework addresses all ACs. ## 2. Owned CI violations — no dismissal `ci_failures.md` opens with machine-extracted violation tables: - **"Violations you must fix (N owned)"** — each row (`check`, `rule`, `path:line`, measured-vs-limit) is in a file changed by this PR's diff. Owned = blocking. Fix it, or dispute it **per item** with `disputed: ` when the gate itself is wrong. - **"Foreign / infra reds (do not chase)"** — reds in files this PR does not touch. Do not fix them here; mention them in the summary. The full uncapped list lives in `ci_violations.json`. In `outputs/response.md`, **list every owned violation with `fixed` or `disputed: `**. A summary that claims the reds are "not caused by this PR" / "unrelated" / "infra" while owned violations are open is mechanically rejected: the leg fails and the no-op loop guard counts the lap. For `dart_format` owned items (rule `dart_format` — the `static` job failed on `dart format --set-exit-if-changed`), the expected fix is `dart format .` on the whole tree, then verify with `dart format --set-exit-if-changed --output=none .` before pushing. ## 3. Already-addressed / invalid threads (audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ## 4. Downgrade protocol — ⚠️→💡 only with a written justification (gh-1351) `review_policy.md` carries the resolved severity table: the tiers whose round is `rework` gate approval and trigger this lap; polish/none tiers do not. Fix in that order (🚨 first, then ⚠️). You may downgrade a **specific** ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only when you write the justification into the census** — both the thread reply and the response summary must state why the finding is NOT real maintainability debt (e.g. the guarded condition is unreachable, the contract is documented elsewhere, the risk is structurally impossible). The next review round honors a justified downgrade: the finding counts 💡 and the cycle converges to APPROVE **without a code change**. - A silent downgrade does not exist — without the written justification the finding stays ⚠️ and the review re-raises it, repeating the loop. - Downgrade the finding, not the conversation: still reply to the thread (the reply IS the justification carrier). - Never downgrade 🚨 BLOCKING — only the reviewer (or the project `reviewPolicy` config) can weaken a blocking finding.

## 5. Opportunistic pickup — cheap 💡/🪶 ride the lap (gh-1352)

While the lap fixes its mandatory set (🚨/⚠️), pick up the cheap findings you pass anyway:

- **Eligible:** 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT findings in the SAME files your mandatory fixes already touch — you are in the file, the change is doc/test-trivial, and the lap budget allows it: `review_policy.md` carries `opportunisticMaxThreads` (default 8) and `opportunisticSameFilesOnly` (default true). Stay inside both.
- **Not eligible (leave for triage):** findings in files the mandatory set does not touch, findings needing >trivial edits, and anything non-local to this PR's diff. Skipping them is correct — the machine triage closes non-picked threads with `wontfix`/`defered` dispositions after the lap lands; do NOT force-fix them here.
- **Bookkeeping:** every picked-up thread still gets its `outputs/review_replies.json` entry; name the fixing commit in the reply so the machine can close it as `fixed: <ref>`. Threads you did not pick up need no reply — triage owns them.
